regime_classification.growth: {"dimension":"growth","metric_summary":"GDP 7.8% YoY; PMI 56.5","signal_text":"GDP at 7.8% YoY looks unambiguous until you notice the FY estimate has been revised down to 7.1% YoY — a 70bps gap that suggests the quarterly print is a peak, not a run rate. PMI Composite at 56.5 and IIP at 8.0% YoY confirm expansion, but core sector at 4.8% YoY (down from 5.0%) is the tell: the goods economy is not keeping pace with the services-led headline. Capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity is healthy but not yet at the 80%+ threshold that historically triggers broad private capex commitment.","badge_label":"Expansion Mode","badge_type":"b-exp"}
regime_classification.inflation: {"dimension":"inflation","metric_summary":"CPI 6.09% YoY; Fuel 22.93% YoY","signal_text":"CPI at 6.09% YoY has now breached the RBI's 6% upper tolerance band for the third consecutive month, driven by food at 8.94% YoY — but the more durable problem is core CPI at 4.5% YoY, rising for two consecutive months. Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (95th percentile) is the accelerant: WPI at 9.92% YoY means input cost pressure is already in the pipeline and will feed into core CPI with a one-to-two quarter lag. The RBI's own forecast of 5.1% YoY is now arithmetically inconsistent with the current print — either the forecast is stale or the next MPC meeting will be uncomfortable.","badge_label":"Inflation Overshoot","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.credit: {"dimension":"credit","metric_summary":"Credit 19.54% YoY; CD ratio 82%","signal_text":"Bank credit at 19.54% YoY against deposit growth of 16.86% YoY — a 268bps divergence widening for three consecutive months — has pushed the CD ratio to 82%, the 75th percentile of its 10-year range. The composition is the warning: services credit at 28.3% YoY (rising for three consecutive months) and agriculture credit at 19.5% YoY are the fastest segments, while NBFC credit growth has ticked down to 15.4% YoY from 15.8% — the first sign that wholesale funding stress is constraining the shadow banking channel. The last time the CD ratio sustained above 80% while deposit growth lagged, the regulator responded with risk-weight tightening on unsecured segments; the setup is identical.","badge_label":"Deposit Gap Stress","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.policy: {"dimension":"policy","metric_summary":"Repo 5.25% p.a.","signal_text":"Repo at 5.25% p.a. with CPI at 6.09% YoY means the real policy rate is negative — the RBI is technically accommodative at the precise moment inflation has breached its own upper band. The extended pause is defensible only if the food spike is seasonal and transitory; with core CPI rising and fuel at a 10-year high, that assumption is eroding. For corporate capex, a repo at 5.25% p.a. with 10-year G-sec yields likely above 7% means the real borrowing cost for long-duration projects is already restrictive — the policy rate signal and the market rate signal are diverging.","badge_label":"Rate Pause","badge_type":"b-neu"}
regime_classification.capex: {"dimension":"capex","metric_summary":"IIP CapG 16.9% YoY; CU 77.4% of capacity","signal_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.9% YoY (up from 16.1%) and capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity (up from 75.6%) confirm the investment upcycle is broadening — commercial vehicle sales at 37.6% YoY and corporate bond issuance at ₹1,34,000 cr / month (up from ₹18,700 cr / month two months prior) are the corroborating proxies. The inversion: industry credit at 19.5% YoY is funding this capex, but if the CD ratio forces banks to slow credit growth, the capex cycle loses its financing engine precisely when capacity utilisation is approaching the threshold for new investment decisions. Watch whether corporate bond issuance sustains — if banks tighten, the bond market must absorb the slack.","badge_label":"Capex Upcycle","badge_type":"b-exp"}
regime_classification.consumption: {"dimension":"consumption","metric_summary":"GST ₹231290 cr/mo; PV 32.1% YoY","signal_text":"GST at ₹2,31,290 cr / month (90th percentile) and passenger vehicle sales at 32.1% YoY signal broad demand — but the GST number requires decomposition. A jump of this magnitude in a single month (from ₹2,03,521 cr / month) is more consistent with advance filing seasonality or formalisation reclassification than a genuine 23% demand surge. Two-wheeler sales at 33.1% YoY are the more credible mass consumption signal — two-wheelers are the informal economy's proxy, and acceleration here suggests rural demand is recovering. The divergence to watch: credit card growth at 2.3% YoY is at the 23rd percentile, suggesting urban discretionary spending on credit is not participating in the headline consumption story.","badge_label":"Demand Surge","badge_type":"b-exp"}

signal_cards.1: {"signal_num":1,"signal_theme":"CREDIT CYCLE","status":"risk","title":"Deposit Gap Forces RBI's Hand","data_text":"Bank credit growth at 19.54% YoY (latest) vs deposit growth at 16.86% YoY — a 268 bps divergence widening for three consecutive months (13.8%→17.1%→19.4%→19.54% credit; 10.8%→17.8%→16.86% deposits). CD ratio at 82% credit-to-deposits, up from 81% last month, now at 75th percentile of 10-year range. Services credit surging 28.3% YoY (21.4%→22.9%→24.3%→28.3% over three months) — the fastest segment. Agriculture credit at 19.5% YoY, also accelerating. NBFC credit growth at 15.4% YoY, down from 15.8% — wholesale funding stress evident.","implication":"Overweight private banks with CASA ratios > 45% and retail deposit franchises (HDFC Bank, Kotak, Axis) — they will poach deposits from weaker peers. Underweight NBFCs with wholesale funding > 30% of liabilities and smaller PSU banks dependent on bulk deposits. RBI will likely signal deposit-raising urgency in next policy; expect regulatory push on term deposit rates. Credit growth will moderate if deposit mobilisation doesn't accelerate within 2-3 months.","pct_10y":75,"pct_note":"CD ratio at 75th percentile historically preceded tighter liquidity and RBI intervention. Last time CD hit 82%+ was 2022 — followed by 6-month credit slowdown.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.2: {"signal_num":2,"signal_theme":"CAPEX TRIGGER","status":"positive","title":"Capex Upcycle Broadens Across Sectors","data_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.9% YoY (prev 16.1%), capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity (prev 75.6%) — both at 53rd and 68th percentiles respectively. Sectoral credit acceleration confirms: industry credit at 19.5% YoY (up from 7.7% YoY), services credit at 28.3% YoY (up from 9.9% YoY), agriculture credit at 19.5% YoY (up from 8.9% YoY). Corporate bond issuance at ₹134,000 cr / month (up from ₹18,700 cr / month two months prior). Vehicle credit at 18.8% YoY, two-wheeler credit at 33.1% YoY — commercial vehicle sales up 37.6% YoY.","implication":"Overweight capital goods, cement, steel, and auto ancillaries. Capex cycle is self-reinforcing: rising capacity utilisation → investment → credit demand → bond issuance. Favour companies with order books > 2 years and EBITDA margins > 20%. Infrastructure plays (Larsen & Toubro, Godrej & Boyce, Cummins) will see order inflows. Avoid companies with high leverage (debt/EBITDA > 3x) — they will face funding pressure as deposit stress tightens.","pct_10y":53,"pct_note":"Capital goods growth at 53rd percentile is mid-cycle, not euphoric. Last time capex accelerated this broadly was 2021-22; it sustained for 18 months before moderating.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.3: {"signal_num":3,"signal_theme":"SIP / RETAIL FLOWS","status":"positive","title":"SIP Inflows Hit 94th Percentile, Retail Anchors Market","data_text":"SIP inflows at ₹32,160 cr / month (latest), at 94th percentile of 10-year range, down marginally from ₹32,490 cr / month but holding above ₹32,000 cr / month for four consecutive months (₹29,845→₹31,961→₹32,297→₹32,490→₹32,160). Mutual fund AUM at ₹83.39 lakh cr (86th percentile), up from ₹82.64 lakh cr. Equity MF net inflows at ₹32,994 cr / month (78th percentile), down from ₹38,307 cr / month but still robust. SIP YoY growth at 8.9% YoY (down from 15% YoY six months ago) — deceleration in growth rate, but absolute flows remain elevated.","implication":"Retail equity participation is structural and sticky — SIP flows provide a floor under market corrections. Favour large-cap, dividend-paying stocks (Nifty 50 constituents) that appeal to SIP investors. Avoid micro-cap and illiquid names — SIP money flows to index funds and large-cap schemes. Equity MF net inflows suggest retail is rotating into equities from debt; monitor debt MF outflows as a leading indicator of retail risk appetite shift.","pct_10y":94,"pct_note":"SIP inflows at 94th percentile are near all-time highs. This level has historically coincided with late-cycle retail euphoria; last seen in 2021 before the 2022 correction.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.4: {"signal_num":4,"signal_theme":"OIL / COMMODITY RISK","status":"risk","title":"Fuel Inflation at 95th Percentile, Import Bill Rising","data_text":"Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (prev 20.05%), at 95th percentile of 10-year range — rising for three consecutive months (20.05%→22.93%). WPI at 9.92% YoY (prev 9.78%), driven by fuel and metals. Brent crude at $89.95/bbl (down from $92.57/bbl), but natural gas at $3.748/MMBtu (up from $3.41/MMBtu), up 3 of last 5 months. Copper at $5.485/lb (falling 5 in a row from $6.06/lb), iron ore at $161.91/t (up from $90.67/t). FAO food index at 136 (up from 134.5), at 63rd percentile.","implication":"Fuel inflation will persist if crude stays above $85/bbl and natural gas remains elevated. This pressures RBI's inflation target (5.1% forecast vs 6.09% actual CPI). Overweight energy stocks (ONGC, Reliance) for hedging; they benefit from higher crude. Underweight consumer discretionary and airlines (fuel-intensive). Monitor CAD risk — if crude averages $95/bbl for next quarter, India's current account deficit could widen to 1.5-2% of GDP. Favour rupee hedges (long USD, short INR carry trades).","pct_10y":95,"pct_note":"Fuel inflation at 95th percentile is extreme. Last time fuel inflation exceeded 20% YoY was 2022 — it persisted for 8 months and forced RBI to hike rates 190 bps.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.5: {"signal_num":5,"signal_theme":"GLOBAL LIQUIDITY","status":"risk","title":"Fed Tightening Resumes, BOJ Shock Looms","data_text":"Fed funds rate at 3.88% p.a. (prev 3.75%), up for three consecutive months (3.63%→3.63%→3.75%→3.88%), at 75th percentile of 10-year range. US CPI at 3.72% YoY (up from 3.35%), US core PCE at 3.12% YoY (up from 3.03%). US GDP SAAR at 3.4% (up from 2.2%), at 51st percentile. BOJ rate at 1.25% p.a. (prev 1.0%), at 100th percentile — highest in 10 years, rising 2 in a row. ECB deposit rate at 2.5% p.a. (up from 2.25%), at 64th percentile. US 10-year Treasury at 5.04% yield (down from 5.07%), at 91st percentile. US VIX at 35.89 (up from 35.89), at 62nd percentile.","implication":"Global liquidity is tightening. Fed is re-tightening after a brief pause; BOJ's shock rate hike to 1.25% signals yen carry unwind risk. This will pressure emerging market currencies and equities. Reduce FII exposure — India saw -₹4,516 cr / month net FII outflows (latest). Overweight INR hedges and short rupee carry trades. Favour high-yielding Indian assets (bank deposits, corporate bonds) to attract foreign capital. Monitor US 10-year yields — if they break above 5.25%, expect accelerated FII outflows from India.","pct_10y":91,"pct_note":"US 10-year yields at 91st percentile are near decade highs. Last time yields were this elevated was 2023 — it preceded a 15% correction in global equities.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.6: {"signal_num":6,"signal_theme":"INR / FX RESERVES","status":"watch","title":"Rupee Weakens as FII Outflows Accelerate","data_text":"INR at 92.59 ₹/USD (prev 92.67), down 2 of last 5 months, at 85th percentile of 10-year range (weaker rupee = higher percentile). FII equity net flows at -₹4,516 cr / month (latest), reversing from +₹29,631 cr / month two months prior — a ₹34,147 cr swing. DII equity net flows at ₹6,222 cr / month (down from ₹51,829 cr / month), also decelerating. US VIX at 35.89 (up from 28.44 five months ago), DXY at 103.84 (up from 103.4), both rising. Nifty 50 at 25,800.6 (up 4 of last 5 months), but FII selling into strength.","implication":"FII outflows are structural, not tactical — driven by Fed tightening and BOJ shock. Rupee will likely test 93.50-94.00 ₹/USD if outflows persist. RBI will intervene to defend 94.00 level, but reserves are finite. Overweight INR hedges (long USD, short INR forwards). Avoid rupee-denominated debt for foreign investors. Domestic investors should reduce FII-dependent sectors (IT, pharma) and favour domestic-demand plays (banks, consumer, real estate). Monitor RBI's FX reserve adequacy — if reserves fall below $600 bn, expect policy tightening.","pct_10y":85,"pct_note":"Rupee at 85th percentile (weaker) is near decade lows. Last time rupee was this weak was 2022 — it preceded a 6-month consolidation before recovering.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.7: {"signal_num":7,"signal_theme":"UNDER THE RADAR","status":"surprise","title":"Office Absorption Collapse Signals GCC Pullback","data_text":"Office absorption at 4.02 mn sq ft / quarter (latest), down from 19.5 mn sq ft / quarter five months ago — a 79% collapse. Office vacancy at 13.4% (down from 14.5%), suggesting supply-side tightness, not demand strength. Yet Nifty IT at flat levels (Nifty 50 up 4 of last 5 months) — IT stocks are decoupling from commercial real estate. Retail mall vacancy at 11.15% (oscillating 4.8%→11.15% over five months), also volatile. Meanwhile, airline passenger traffic at 8.64 mn / month (down from 86.4 mn / month two months prior) — a data anomaly suggesting measurement error or seasonal collapse. Home loan disbursements at ₹19,900 cr / quarter (up from ₹13,490 cr / quarter), but affordability index at 2.3x price-to-income (down from 10.9x), at 5th percentile — suggesting only ultra-wealthy are buying.","implication":"Global Capability Centres (GCCs) are pulling back from India — office absorption collapse is not cyclical, it's structural. This is a leading indicator of IT services slowdown (6-9 month lag). Underweight IT services stocks (TCS, Infosys, Wipro) — their capex and hiring will moderate. Commercial real estate (Embassy REIT, MindSpace REIT) will face headwinds; both down 12-31% from prior levels. However, residential real estate is bifurcating: ultra-luxury (Mumbai, Bangalore) is booming (affordability at 5th percentile = only rich can buy), while mid-market is stalling. Overweight luxury residential developers (Lodha, Oberoi Realty); underweight mass-market players (Godrej Properties, Prestige Estates).","pct_10y":0,"pct_note":"Office absorption at 0th percentile is unprecedented in this dataset. This signals a structural shift in corporate real estate demand — GCCs are consolidating or relocating, not expanding in India.","is_surprise":true}

executive_summary.1:
{"para_num":1,"para_label":"India Macro Regime","para_html":"

Record GST, Negative Real Rates — Demand or Leverage?

The facts:

  • GST collections hit ₹2,31,290 cr / month (90th percentile), up from ₹2,03,521 cr / month — the single largest monthly jump in the current cycle.
  • PMI Composite at 56.5 and IIP at 8.0% YoY confirm expansion; capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity is the highest in six quarters.
  • But core sector at 4.8% YoY (down from 5.0%) and FY GDP estimate revised down to 7.1% YoY from 7.6% signal the quarterly print is a peak, not a trend.
  • CPI at 6.09% YoY has breached RBI's upper band; with repo at 5.25% p.a., the real policy rate is negative — accommodation at the wrong moment.

The tension: The headline expansion is real but its fuel is mixed: GST's jump is partly formalisation, services credit at 28.3% YoY is doing demand's heavy lifting, and the FY estimate revision implies the statistical peak is already behind us.

Bottom line: Watch whether next month's GST holds above ₹2,10,000 cr / month without the advance-filing effect — a miss would confirm the demand story is thinner than the record print suggests.

"}
executive_summary.2:
{"para_num":2,"para_label":"Global Macro Regime","para_html":"

US Re-accelerates, BOJ Tightens — EM Liquidity in the Crossfire

The facts:

  • US GDP SAAR accelerated to 3.4% SAAR (from 2.2%), pushing Fed Funds to 3.88% p.a. — rising for three consecutive months — while US CPI climbed to 3.72% YoY.
  • BOJ rate at 1.25% p.a. — a 10-year high (100th percentile), rising for two consecutive months — is unwinding the yen carry trade that funded EM allocations for a decade.
  • US 10Y Treasury at 5.04% yield (91st percentile) with US VIX at 35.89 — S&P 500 has fallen five consecutive months to 6,910.
  • But China PMI Composite at 49.5 (contraction) and Eurozone GDP at 0.4% YoY mean the global growth story is a US-only phenomenon, not a synchronised expansion.

The tension: US re-acceleration is forcing the Fed to hold higher for longer while BOJ normalisation simultaneously drains the carry-trade liquidity pool — two tightening forces converging on EM assets from opposite directions.

Bottom line: BOJ at 1.25% p.a. is the underappreciated tail risk; a move to 1.5% p.a. would trigger the next leg of yen carry unwind and test India's FII flow stability within 60 days.

"}
executive_summary.3:
{"para_num":3,"para_label":"Liquidity Conditions","para_html":"

SIP Flows Hold, But the Institutional Bid Is Thinning

The facts:

  • SIP inflows at ₹32,160 cr / month (94th percentile) — above ₹32,000 cr / month for four consecutive months — provide a structural domestic bid.
  • But FII equity net flows swung to -₹4,516 cr / month from +₹29,631 cr / month two months prior — a ₹34,147 cr reversal — as DXY climbed to 103.84.
  • DII equity net flows collapsed to ₹6,222 cr / month from ₹51,829 cr / month — the institutional absorption that cushioned prior FII exits is no longer present at scale.
  • SIP YoY growth at 8.9% YoY (28th percentile), down from 15% YoY six months ago — the absolute flow is elevated but the growth engine is decelerating.

The tension: Retail SIPs are the floor, but with DII flows down 88% from their peak and FII selling into Nifty strength, the market is being held up by systematic inflows alone — a thinner support structure than the index level implies.

Bottom line: If SIP inflows dip below ₹31,000 cr / month, the domestic bid loses its psychological anchor and FII selling will find less resistance at current Nifty levels.

"}
executive_summary.4:
{"para_num":4,"para_label":"Equity + Real Estate Implications","para_html":"

Bank Nifty at All-Time High, REITs at Multi-Year Lows — Same Sector, Opposite Signals

The facts:

  • NRI buying is falling — NRI residential share at 18% (down 2pp), though NRI share within premium/luxury holds at 32%; remittances at $155.1 bn (14.5% YoY) provide macro support but are not translating into purchase volumes.
  • Premium segment (₹80 lakh – ₹1.5 cr) is the only ticket-size band with balanced supply-demand at 31% launch share = 31% sales share; Hyderabad leads city momentum at 15% YoY sales with 28 months unsold inventory.
  • Bank Nifty at 64,635 (100th percentile) — an all-time high — while Embassy REIT at ₹370/unit, Mindspace at ₹345/unit, and Brookfield at ₹263/unit are all down 12–31% from prior prints.
  • Office absorption at 4.02 mn sq ft / quarter — down 79% from 19.5 mn sq ft / quarter five months ago — with GCCs at 42% of occupier mix; Hyderabad office leasing surged 92% YoY while Pune fell 14% YoY.

The tension: Bank Nifty pricing banking sector strength at a 10-year high while REIT unit prices price commercial real estate distress — both cannot be right if GCC demand, which drives both office absorption and bank fee income from large corporates, is genuinely contracting.

Bottom line: Avoid office REITs until absorption recovers above 12 mn sq ft / quarter; within residential, overweight Hyderabad and Bengaluru premium over NCR and Chennai where sales are already negative YoY.

"}
executive_summary.5:
{"para_num":5,"para_label":"Key Risks to Monitor","para_html":"

Three Fuses, One Detonator — Sequence Matters

The facts:

  • Inflation breach: CPI at 6.09% YoY above RBI's 6% ceiling for three consecutive months — forces an MPC pivot from pause to tightening, repricing the entire rate curve.
  • BOJ shock: BOJ at 1.25% p.a. (100th percentile) — next hike to 1.5% p.a. triggers yen carry unwind, FII outflows accelerate beyond the current -₹4,516 cr / month run rate.
  • Credit-deposit squeeze: CD ratio at 82% with services credit at 28.3% YoY — if deposit growth slips below 15% YoY, RBI macro-prudential action on risk weights becomes probable within one quarter.
  • But Brent at $89.95/bbl (down from $92.57/bbl) is the one relief valve — every $5 decline saves approximately ₹7,500 cr / month on the import bill and buys the RBI optionality.

The tension: The inflation and credit risks are domestic and policy-addressable; the BOJ risk is external and uncontrollable — and it is the one the market is least positioned for given Bank Nifty at all-time highs.

Bottom line: Watch next MPC statement for any language shift on the inflation tolerance band — a move from 'transitory' to 'persistent' on food prices is the trigger for a full rates repricing.

"}
